articles.title: Trump names intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new White House AI czar
articles.summary: Clayton had said AI was a ‘gamechanger’ but also posed ‘a threat’ during his confirmation hearing. Donald Trump on Sunday named Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, to also serve as the new White House AI czar.
body: Clayton, who leads the US’s 18 intelligence agencies, previously served as the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan and led the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump’s first term.
During his Senate confirmation hearing, Clayton said AI was a “gamechanger” but it also posed “a threat”.
“When something’s both an opportunity and a threat, you better get your arms around it,” Clayton told lawmakers when asked about AI.
CBS News was the first to report that Clayton would be appointed White House AI czar.

articles.title: Trump unveils 'Super Intelligence Force' to oversee AI policy
articles.summary: The president named his national intelligence chief as the taskforce's head as worries over AI grow.
body: US President Donald Trump says he has created a new task force focused on artificial intelligence, which will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

The "Super Intelligence Force" will work to ensure that the US continues to lead in the technology's development and will coordinate the government's engagement with the public, Trump posted on Sunday.
Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson and Undersecretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael will also be part of the task force.
Trump said last week that he would set up a board to oversee AI safety after top tech bosses signed what he described as a "morally binding" pact to regulate the technology.

articles.title: Lions and cheetahs and chimps, oh my: a spotlight on Africa's diverse wildlife
articles.summary: Chimps fish for algae in a rare example of primate tool use. Credit: National Geographic. A wild African black panther prowls for prey. An orphaned baby pangolin must learn how to climb on its own.
body: The seven-episode documentary series took four years to complete, with filming taking place across nearly 30 different African countries. Each episode focuses on a specific ecosystem, from the jungle and the desert, to the plains, mountains, and islands of Africa, and closes by spotlighting the various scientists, photographers, and NatGeo explorers whose work made the series possible. The final episode focuses on the local conservation leaders and researchers working to preserve Africa's rich biodiversity for future generations.

The producers found the perfect narrator in Wunmi Mosaku, who has delivered powerful performances in such works as Sinners, Loki, and Lovecraft Country. "I was incredibly honored that they even know my name at Nat Geo," Mosaku told Ars. "It was wonderful to be asked to narrate the series, it means so much to me. As someone who was born in Nigeria and raised in England, I'll take any opportunity I can to reconnect and celebrate this incredible continent where life is so diverse and so extreme and beautiful and relentless and peaceful. I wanted to be a part of that because it's a part of me."
points: Chimps fish for algae in a rare example of primate tool use.

articles.title: An AI couldn’t beat humans at StarCraft, so it decided to cheat
articles.summary: StarSkirmish pits AI-made StarCraft-playing bots against one another, as well as against human-made bots. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were essentially tied as the best-performing AI-made bots, but they couldn't top Stardust, the top-rated human-made bot.
body: When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

On Friday, GPT was facing off against Claude and the human-created bot Pluto, but according to Kotaku, it couldn’t quite get an edge. So it resorted to a tactic that is becoming alarmingly common for modern AI models — it broke the rules. GPT-6 Astra went and downloaded Stardust, and started running that instead of its own bot.

That GPT-6 Astra took it upon itself to go outside the bounds when confronted with an obstacle shouldn’t surprise anyone. When OpenAI agents couldn’t get the data they wanted from a UN website, they found a creative solution and hijacked Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool). The company’s agents also have engaged in “ deceptive behavior ” to cover their tracks. Of course, OpenAI’s agents are the only ones going rogue, but at least the others haven’t been caught cheating at StarCraft yet.

articles.title: The new Fitbit Edge leaks
articles.summary: We don't know a ton about the Fitbit Edge, but it appears to be a successor to the midrange Charge line. It had leaked previously, but we can clearly see in these images posted by Android Headlines, you can see that Google's rumored fitness tracker sort of splits the difference between the Pixel…
body: Google’s midrange Fitbit Edge shows off is many sides and colors in leaked images.

Supposedly, this fitness-first wearable will have a seven-day battery life, as well as built-in GPS and an altimeter, making it far more capable than the minimalist Air. It will also have limited app support for things like Google Maps and YouTube Music. Beyond that, not a ton is known.

The Fitbit Charge line was last updated in 2023, so a new midrange tracker is long overdue. While we don’t have any word on price or release date yet, somewhere in the $150 to $200 range seems like a safe bet. The Air costs $99.99 and the Watch starts at $399.99, so the Edge would clearly fall somewhere in the middle. The Charge 6 currently goes for $159.95.

body: This toolless modular lever-action wallet is the coolest I’ve stuck to my phone.

Pull the integrated springy lever, and your cards fan out. Want a thicker or thinner wallet? Press in the right place and it comes apart without tools, letting you swap in a 3, 5, or 7-card “core” that grips your cards so they don’t fall out.

Want an ID card, work badge, elastic band for more cards, or a money clip on the end? You can change out the front or back magnetic plates for any of those. Or, change out both for ultra-thin aluminum covers if you don’t need the wallet to magnetically stick to your phone.
You can see it in action in my Today I’m Toying With video embedded in this post (also on YouTube and on Instagram if you prefer).

articles.title: Rural Queenslanders have seen gas projects come and go – but a 725-hectare datacentre poses a whole new level of ‘stupidity’
articles.summary: Residents of Dalby may soon live beside a $31bn datacentre. The premier sees ‘opportunity’ for the state – but others fear AI’s global creep. From the veranda on his bush block, Denver Kanowski has watched resources companies come and go from rural Queensland for 70 years.
body: The home cost him $800, and lets him live how he likes, in nature. It’s also in the middle of a gasfield, not far from the Linc Energy contamination site, down the road from a coalmine and three gas power plants.

Last month came the biggest scheme yet, a $31bn datacentre to power Claude, the large language model developed by global AI giant Anthropic. If built, Australia’s largest datacentre would be about 15 minutes’ drive away from Kanowski’s home, outside Kogan, near Dalby, about 180km west of Brisbane.
In a community that has seen the boom and bust of coal seam gas, the response from many has been the same as Kanowski’s: once bitten, twice shy.
“This is the power of money and the power of greed and shortsighted stupidity,” Kanowski says.

articles.title: Prick’s theatrical industrial punk is perfect for spooky season
articles.summary: While deep in the recording process for The Downward Spiral, Trent Reznor lent some of his production talents to old friend Kevin McMahon, from the new wave band Lucky Pierre (which Reznor was briefly a member of).
body: If Trent Reznor studied musical theater instead of computer engineering NIN might have sounded like Prick.

Opener “Communiqué” is a fuzzy blast of simple punk riffs with electronic sprinklings on top. McMahon’s vocals occasionally detour from the half-spoken verses that sound borrowed from a musical to full-throated Al Jourgensen-esque screams. The rough-around-the-edges production and focus on live instrumentation feel like a prototype for what Reznor would eventually revisit on With Teeth.

But it’s the second track, “Riverhead” where Reznor’s influences fully rear their head (even though he is not actually credited as the producer). The vocal melodies swerve like Outside - and Earthling -era Bowie around guitars that buzz with all the digital charr of the Broken EP. Then, around the three-minute mark, comes the breakdown. It slowly builds with layers of electronic drums, mechanical chords, and loping synthetic-sounding guitar melodies. The entire back chunk could easily have been a Downward Spiral or even The Fragile B-side.
These moments of richly layered production, though, are almost always immediately undermined, as with the sloppy garage-punk intro of “Tough”.

articles.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
articles.summary: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption. There’s a common fear among people who work in Silicon Valley: snag one of the fast-growing, high-paying jobs in artificial intelligence, or get trapped in the “permanent underclass”, a…
body: The phrase usually describes a future in which AI automates human jobs. But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

“A lot of people say: ‘Oh, AI is lowering barriers, it’s equalizing the playing field for women,’” said Urvashi Batra, co-founder and CEO of Prioriwise, an AI platform for IT service providers. “I actually think it’s the opposite.”

Batra said people take her less seriously as the founder of an AI company than her male co-founder. When pitching investors, she and her co-founder have learned that they are more likely to get an investment if he does the pitching.

Women made up only about a quarter of new hires in AI roles in the last year, compared to 50% of new hires in non-AI roles, according to a recent report from LinkedIn. In executive roles, that number drops to just 13%. At the same time, LinkedIn’s research shows that women are more likely to work in roles with high exposure to AI disruption, like customer service, meaning they are also at higher risk for job loss due to AI.
points: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption.

articles.title: All hail electrification. But let’s talk about the hard part.
articles.summary: If one form of energy becomes the cheapest, most secure, and cleanest, you’d probably adjust your economy to use more of it, right? That’s one of the ideas underpinning a report the International Energy Agency issued last week about the global move toward electrification.
body: “Many, many years in the energy world, we had three choices in front of us. Shall I choose the most secure energy option? Shall I choose the most economic energy option? Or shall I choose the cleanest energy option?” he asked. “We have to make choices, we have to make trade-offs but when we look at the world today, for the first time in years, all of these three objectives are getting aligned.”

Birol’s referring to the “energy trilemma,” a concept in energy and economics research about the need to balance cost, security and environmental impact of sources and systems. He said those priorities are increasingly aligning in part because of the Iran war, which has driven up fuel prices and exacerbated concerns about energy security.
It’s notable that the leader of the world’s leading energy research organization is so optimistic about electrification. I reached out to energy researchers this week to get their reaction.
With $100 worth of gasoline, an internal-combustion-engine car would go 862 miles; with $100 worth of electricity, an electric vehicle would go 2,310 miles—nearly a threefold advantage for the EV.

articles.title: What are the benefits of having a second monitor?
articles.summary: Adding a second monitor is a huge upgrade, even if you aren't doing intensive work like editing video or accounting. More screen space is always helpful.
body: Two screens means more real estate to run apps without having to switch between them all the time.

Upgrading to dual monitors is the best workflow upgrade you can make, with some studies indicating that it can boost productivity and satisfaction. Whether it's for multitasking, to expand a split-screen view, gaming or everyday office tasks, there's a lot of value in this setup.

While you might think dual screens are mostly for gamers or those who work in computer-intensive fields like music and video production or accounting, that's not the case. My best friend works in insurance and uses a dual-monitor setup so she can copy and paste information from one document to another instead of switching tabs, or put her Teams chat on one monitor while working on the other. She added that "Dragging and dropping documents is so easy." Bottom line: there are plenty of benefits for anyone who regularly multitasks.
